ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: image1 is a schematic diagram of a straightened belt, with one row of claspable holes on the left side and the right side respectively; in the figure, arrows mark that the distance between two adjacent holes is 2 cm. image2 shows the belt clasped through these holes after being formed into a ring shape. Reasoning: The problem says the belt has 5 clasping methods, which can be understood as from the 1st hole to the 5th hole. If changing from the 1st hole to the 5th hole, there are altogether 4 adjacent-hole intervals in between. Each interval is 2 cm, so the length difference is 4 × 2 cm = 8 cm.

raw_record.question_text: A belt can be joined together in 5 different ways. How many $\mathrm{cm}$ is the belt longer if it is only closed in the first hole instead of in all 5 holes?

method.method_draft: Read the straight-belt diagram: there are 5 possible holes/settings, and the picture marks the distance between adjacent holes as 2 cm. From the text, compare closing the belt in the first hole with closing it in the fifth/last available hole. Count the gaps between hole 1 and hole 5: there are 4 equal gaps. Multiply 4 by 2 cm to get the length difference, 8 cm.
